The longer that I do this less I believe in supplements in general. A grocery store and a gym membership is all that's required. For more results and serious lifting, add gear. In terms of cost, $40-45 of Creatine HCL and Testosterone Enanthate will both last 1-2 months. Of course the testosterone will produce much better results.

Also, all of these "studies" always use DYELs and then report back some astronomical number like "the creatine group grew 80% more!!" That's all fine and dandy, but what happens after 2-3 bulk/cut cycles? Oh that's right, everyone ends up scratching the ceiling of the genetic limit and the supplement company made money.

I don't know where you're getting your creatine or if you're getting some fancy shit, but creatine is one of the cheapest nutrients you can buy that also has a large effect on gains. It's been proven to have significant effect when compared with non supplemented use. It's a standard for a reason. But I agree most supplements have negligible, if any real effect. And for anyone who isn't a competitive builder in the top physique there's no reason to use any thing besides protein and creatine. Pre workout works kind of, but the majority of its effect is likely merely just from the caffeine, so nothing worth paying extra for unless you replace energy drinks with them

What I'm saying is that two natties will both grind up against the same ceiling of genetic potential after years of training. Creatine will no doubt get you to that max faster, but you'll be stuck there either way. At that point, you're either happy with where you are or you get gear. Now you have to ask yourself if the tradeoff was worth it. For something as dirt cheap as creation monohydrate? Maybe. But you can also get a 1-2 months of test for the same price, which will give you more gains than 10 drums of creatine.
